aiPlanner.metaDescription: Motir AI Planner asks until it is clear what you are building, then drafts the whole plan: every piece of work, in order, with who does it. Nothing starts until you approve it.
aiPlanner.headline: First the what. Then the whole plan.
aiPlanner.lede: Describe what you want to build. The planner asks until it is clear what you mean, because it won't plan a guess. Then it reads what already exists and drafts the whole plan: every piece of work, in the order it has to happen, with who does it. Nothing starts until you approve it.

steps.headline: It thinks it through with you

items.title: Asks until it's clear
items.body: If it isn't yet clear what you're building, it asks. It won't plan until it knows.

items.title: Reads what exists
items.body: Your repositories, documents and board, or a project you bring from Jira, Linear or Plane. It plans from where you are, not from a blank page.

items.title: Drafts the whole plan
items.body: Every piece of work from the big goals down to the small steps, each with who does it and what it waits on.

items.title: Checks its own work
items.body: Every plan is checked before you see it, so what reaches you is a plan that can be built.

gate.headline: You approve the plan
gate.body: Nothing reaches the board until you say so. Ask for changes in plain words: move this later, split that, drop the export. Each round is a new turn, and the plan keeps every version and the reason it changed.
gate.motirPlans: Create an account to see what Motir planned for itself

items.title: The whole tree
items.body: Epics, stories, tasks and subtasks, from the goal down to the step.

items.title: Who does it
items.body: Each work item goes to an agent or to a person. Work only a person can do is a manual task.

items.title: The order
items.body: What waits on what, so each piece starts the moment it can.

items.title: The difficulty
items.body: A level on every work item, so it runs on a model that fits it.

items.title: The kind of work
items.body: Code, design, tests, documents, research, review: each kind is marked.

items.title: The schedule
items.body: Once you approve: sprints, a backlog and a roadmap.

learns.headline: It learns from every mistake
learns.body: When an agent can't build what the plan asked for, Motir first checks whether the plan was wrong or was changed after you approved it. A real planning mistake becomes a lesson, or strengthens one. Every new plan reads the lessons first, and a lesson that hasn't been needed for 90 days retires.
lessons: Put sign-in before anything that needs a user
Keep an email provider choice a manual task
Split a story that needs two kinds of work
Plan the empty state with the screen

close.headline: Bring the idea.
close.body: The planner does the rest of the thinking with you.

aiDebugging.metaDescription: Bugs from production, from your team and from agents mid-run arrive traced to the code and planned. Motir AI names the likely cause, checks for a card that covers it, and resolves the Sentry error when the bug is done.
aiDebugging.headline: Every bug arrives traced to the code and planned.
aiDebugging.lede: From production, from someone on your team, or from an agent in the middle of a run: each bug lands with what done looks like, where in the code to start and what might be wrong. You decide who fixes it.

plan.headline: Possible causes, never a guess passed off as the answer
plan.body: The planner reads the stack trace against your repositories and writes the bug like a teammate would: what done looks like, where in the code to start, and why it matters. Likely causes are listed as possibilities to rule in or out, and when the trace can't be matched to your code, the bug says so.

fix.headline: Fix it by hand, or hand it to an agent
fix.body: A planned bug is an ordinary work item. Fix it yourself, or let an agent pick up the Bugs folder and open a pull request for each one. You review and merge, the bug is done, and the error is resolved in Sentry.

setup.headline: Connect once, choose what counts
setup.body: Connect your Sentry organization, then choose which of its projects send errors to this board. For each one, set the lowest level that counts, and whether finishing a bug resolves the error and whether Sentry's assignee carries over.

sources.headline: Three ways in, one kind of bug

items.title: Describe it to Motir AI
items.body: Tell it what's broken. It reads the code, names the likely cause, checks whether a card already covers it, then writes exactly one: a new bug or a note on the existing one.

items.title: From production
items.body: Connect Sentry and each new error becomes a bug with its stack trace. When it happens again, the count goes up, not the pile.

items.title: From an agent run
items.body: An agent that finds a bug outside its own work files it, with what it saw and where, and keeps going.

describe.headline: Say what's broken. Motir AI traces it.
describe.body: Describe the bug in your own words, or report it and hand it over. Motir AI reads your code and your plan, names the likely cause, and checks for a card that already covers it. It writes one thing and says exactly what: a new bug in Triage with the diagnosis, or the diagnosis added to the card that already tracks it. If it can't trace the bug to the code, it writes nothing.

production.headline: Errors arrive as bugs, with the evidence
production.body: Each new Sentry error becomes one bug work item with its exception, stack trace and a link back. When the bug is done, Motir resolves the error in Sentry. If it comes back, a new bug is filed, linked to the old one.

runs.headline: Agents report what they find
runs.body: An agent building one work item that hits a bug somewhere else doesn't stop and doesn't hide it. It files the bug with what it saw, notes the run it was found in, and carries on with its own work. The run lists every bug it filed.

agentFleet.metaDescription: Motir's hosted agents work every ready item of your plan at once, each on its own machine with a model that fits the job. Start them yourself or let Motir Project Manager keep them busy.
agentFleet.headline: Your whole plan, worked in parallel.
agentFleet.lede: Motir's hosted agents take every work item that is ready and work them at the same time, each on a fresh machine with its own branch and pull request. Start them yourself, or let Motir Project Manager keep them busy, and the project moves on every front at once.

parallel.headline: One machine for every ready work item
parallel.body: Everything that can start, starts. Each run claims its work item, so no two agents ever take the same one, and works it on a machine of its own. A story runs its pieces in the order they depend on each other. The more work is ready, the more runs at once.

pm.headline: Motir Project Manager keeps the fleet busy
pm.body: Hand the project to Motir Project Manager and it starts a run the moment a work item is ready, picks the model, and brings you only what needs your decision: the pull requests, the designs, the plans.

models.eyebrow: The right model for each job
models.headline: Every work item has a difficulty. It picks the model.
models.body: The planner gives every task, subtask and bug a difficulty: how hard the work is to get right, not how big it is. A one-line change to lock ordering can be high while a large rename is trivial. The fleet reads it to choose the model, so a rename doesn't pay for the strongest model and a data migration never runs on the cheapest.

items.title: Trivial
items.body: Mechanical work with an unambiguous spec: a rename, a copy change, a config flip. Runs on a faster, cheaper model.

items.title: Low
items.body: Routine work that follows a pattern the code already has, like a new field through an existing form. Runs on a faster, cheaper model.

items.title: Medium
items.body: Real design choices across several files or services, or a bug whose cause isn't known yet. Runs on the strongest model.

items.title: High
items.body: Work where a subtle mistake is costly: concurrency, security, a migration on live data. Runs on the strongest model.

items.title: Your choice
items.body: Set your own model for any level in the project, or pick one for a single run, from Claude, DeepSeek, GLM and Qwen.

items.title: Pay for what runs
items.body: Billed in credits for model calls and machine time. Nothing runs, nothing is billed.

howItWorks.metaDescription: The workflow behind “vibe the project”: AI planning, the plan gate, agent runs, the merge gate, repair, the learning loop and the project's memory.
howItWorks.headline: Vibing the project.
howItWorks.lede: Every Motir project runs through the same instrument. The modules are Motir and its agents. The knobs and switches are yours: nothing moves forward until a person turns them.

stage.shellCaption: Vibe coding is one knob. Here are three.

howItWorks.toyTitle: Vibe coding drawn as a toy with one knob
howItWorks.toyDesc: A small plastic gadget with a single knob: type a prompt and out comes a heap of files, tangled in imports, with a circular import among them. Changing one line in one file breaks seven others. There is no plan, no board, no review and no memory; everything else is left to you. Scrolling replaces it with the full Motir instrument.

toy.foot: Prompt in. Code out. The rest is up to you.

howItWorks.shellTitle: Motir as one instrument with three controls
howItWorks.shellDesc: A closed synthesizer case. Its front panel has three controls joined by patch cables: the idea input where you type what you want, the Motir plan knob that turns it into a plan, and the Motir build knob that builds it. Scrolling opens the case to show the modules inside.

shell.foot: Your idea in · working software out

howItWorks.rackTitle: The Motir workflow as a rack of modules
howItWorks.rackDesc: Your idea is patched into the planner, then into a knob where you approve the plan, then the board, then an agent run, then a knob where you review and merge, then Done. Manual tasks go from the board to Done. An agent run can log a bug it finds into the Bugs folder and keep going. A repair module loops failed runs back into the agent run. A learning loop runs from the agent run through a verdict, a re-plan and the lesson library back into the planner. A memory bank along the bottom holds designs, decisions, docs, lessons, run history, revisions and who decided what. A switch on the rack flips between vibe coding, which keeps only your idea and the agent run, and vibing the project, which uses every module.
howItWorks.schematicTitle: Motir's architecture as a circuit schematic
howItWorks.schematicDesc: The services behind Motir drawn as components joined by signal lines. In the public zone: motir.co, the design system package, the agent shell relay, motir-core (web and REST API, the MCP server, sign-in, and the worker with its job queue) and motir-ai, the planner. In the private zone: motir-gateway, which meters every model call, and the code graph service. In the fleet: the agent host, the agent runner, the index runner and the CI runner, all booted on demand. In the data zone: Postgres and the file store. Outside: your browser, your own agent connected over MCP, the payments provider, the model providers and your code host.

rack.engineSub: Blue modules do the work. Orange controls are yours.

vibe.label: Mode
vibe.note: Flip it: vibe coding is two of the modules

howItWorks.modulesLede: Each module in the drawing above, up close. Hover one to find it in the drawing.

modules.label: [01] AI planning
modules.title: From a prompt to a plan
paras: Start with a sentence, a repository, or an import from Jira, Linear or Plane. The planner reads what exists, including a code graph of your repositories, and asks follow-up questions where the request is ambiguous.
It drafts epics, stories, tasks and subtasks, each with a type, an executor, a size and its `blocked_by` edges. `validate_plan` checks the tree before you see it.

modules.label: [02] You · plan gate
modules.title: You approve the plan
paras: Nothing lands on the board until a person approves the plan. Ask for changes in plain words; each round is a new turn, and the plan's history keeps every version and why it changed.

modules.label: [03] Work items
modules.title: The board
paras: The approved plan becomes work items with sprints, a backlog and a roadmap. Each work item's executor is `agent` or `human`.
Manual tasks (an account, a secret, a DNS record, a release sign-off) are walked through one step at a time by `motir guide`.

modules.label: [04] Agent run
modules.title: Agents build
paras: An agent takes the next ready work item (`motir next` or `motir run <KEY>`), claims it, builds on its own branch and opens one pull request per repository, linked to the work item.
A bug it finds outside its own work item doesn't stop the run: the agent root-causes it, files it with `motir log bug` into the Bugs folder as a work item of its own, and keeps going.
Each run records the agent harness, the model, every step and the outcome. Agents connect over MCP, on your machine or Motir's hosted agents.

modules.label: [05] You · merge gate
modules.title: You review and merge
paras: The work item moves to `Implemented` and the agent publishes How to test. Stories get an acceptance video recorded in CI. You review, approve and merge; the merge closes the work item. Nothing reaches `Done` without a person.

modules.label: [06] Repair
modules.title: When runs break
paras: A red or conflicting pull request is repaired on its own branch with `motir fix`, up to five attempts. A run that died (a laptop closed, a sandbox lost) is resumed with `motir continue` on the branch it left.
Bugs logged along the way wait in the Bugs folder; `motir fix bugs` works through them, oldest first.

modules.label: [07] Learning loop
modules.title: The planner learns
paras: An agent that can't build a work item first asks whether it is still what the approved plan approved (`get_approved_shape_verdict`), so a later edit isn't blamed on the planner. If the plan was wrong, it is re-planned and the change is recorded with its reason.
The mistake becomes a lesson, or reinforces one; with no rule to cover it, a planning bug is filed. The next plan reads the lessons first. Lessons that don't recur for 90 days retire.

modules.label: [08] Memory
modules.title: The project remembers
paras: Designs, decision pages, docs, lessons, plan revisions and every run's history live next to the work items. You, a new teammate or the next agent can pick the project up months later without anyone explaining it again.

howToUse.metaTitle: How to use Motir: one part, two, or all three
howToUse.metaDescription: Motir has three parts: a planner, the project management tool in the middle, and an agent runner. Use the middle with your own planner and agents over MCP, add the Motir planner, or let Motir run all three.
howToUse.headline: Use one part, two, or all three.
howToUse.lede: Motir has three parts. The project management tool sits in the middle and holds the plan. The planner plans into it. The agent runner takes tasks from it and builds them. Any part you'd rather run yourself, you can.

parts.name: Motir AI Planner
parts.body: Turns your idea into epics, stories and tasks, and files them into the project once you approve.

parts.name: Motir Project Management
parts.body: The board, backlog, sprints and roadmap. Every planner and every agent, yours or Motir's, works through it.

parts.name: Motir Agent Fleet
parts.body: Takes each ready task, runs an agent on it on its own machine, in parallel with the others, and opens the pull request.

ways.label: 1 · Project management only
ways.title: Your planner, your agents, Motir in the middle.
paras: Use Motir as the project management tool and keep everything around it your own.

Planning over MCP stays open. Write your own planner, a script or an agent, and it files the plan into Motir with the same tools Motir's planner uses: `create_plan`, `add_plan_items` and `validate_plan`. Before Motir AI Planner was built, Motir planned itself this way too, with a script called plan.py.

Your agents connect over MCP. Each one takes the next ready task with `claim_next_ready`, runs it, and reports back with `close_work_item_run`. Motir keeps track of who has which task and what shipped.

paras: Add Motir AI Planner. Give it your idea: it asks what it needs to know, lays the work out as epics, stories and tasks, and files the plan into the project once you approve it.
The building stays yours. Your own orchestration takes ready tasks from Motir over MCP, hands each one to an agent, and reports the result back.

You decide at the gates: approve the plan, then review what gets merged.

explainer.metaTitle: How the calculation works — Motir AI
explainer.metaDescription: Where Motir AI's credit estimate and the plan it recommends come from: what you enter, model categories, credits per item, the range, the plan ladder up to Host and the larger pool plans, and who pays for what.
explainer.headline: How the calculation works
explainer.lede: Where the credit estimate and the plan it recommends come from — the same figures the price page and the calculator use.
explainer.figuresUnavailableNote: Live figures are not available right now, so this page explains each step in words. The price page shows every plan with its price.
explainer.entryLink: Want to know where these numbers come from? <link>How the calculation works</link>

s1.title: What you enter
s1.ranges: Two ranges a month: items you plan in Motir, and items you run on Motir's runner.
s1.ownAgent: An item you run on your own agent — Claude Code, Codex — through Motir's MCP or CLI uses no running credits. If you run everything yourself, enter zero runs and you are quoted planning only.

s2.title: Model categories
s2.body: Planning and running each take a category, not a specific model. Example models come from Motir's live model list, so no model here is a promise.
s2.categoriesFigureFree: The category names come from Motir's live model list.
s2.split: Two selected categories share the estimate 50/50; three share it 33/33/33.

s3.title: Credits per item
s3.body: A reference amount of work per item, times the live price of the chosen model, times a lane factor for planning and for running. The reference is the typical work one item takes; it is not a price.
s3.laneFactors: Planning and running each carry their own lane factor.

s4.title: The range
s4.body: Real token use varies, so low items are counted at 1× and high items at 2×.
s4.caption: Always a range, never a single number.

s5.title: The recommendation
s5.body: The calculator recommends the cheapest of these plans that covers your high end. Each is a plan of its own.
s5.maxX2FigureFree: A plan of its own, twice Max's credits
s5.topUp: A small shortfall is covered by a top-up estimate at {price} for {credits} credits.
s5.topUpFigureFree: A small shortfall is covered by a top-up estimate at the catalog's top-up rate.
s5.largerBody: When your high end is past Max ×2 and a sensible top-up, the calculator offers a larger pool plan sized from your own estimate, on the same per-credit basis as the ladder, and you buy it yourself.
s5.largerFrom: Larger plans start from {credits} credits a month.
s5.largerFromFigureFree: Larger plans start well above Host's credits.

s6.title: Host, and what a plan includes beyond credits
s6.hostBody: A regular plan above Max ×2. You buy it from the price page; the calculator never recommends it, because what it buys is not only credits. A Host organization gets three AWS accounts of its own:

accounts.name: Account 3
accounts.use: Shared by indexing and hosted agents

s6.sharedFloor: Until AWS grants those accounts' capacity, a Host organization runs on Motir's shared capacity with Max's limits, and its admin sees each account's state.
s6.largerPlans: The larger pool plans start well above Host and also carry AWS accounts of their own.
s6.otherPlans: Every other plan runs on Motir's shared capacity, with how many agent runs and hosted agents it may have at once set by its plan.

s7.title: Who pays for what
s7.organization: Every AI plan — Standard, Pro, Max, Max ×2, Host and the larger pool plans — and every top-up belongs to the organization. Its credits are shared by the whole organization; an AI plan is not priced by how many people use it and has no quantity.
s7.includedSeat: Every AI plan includes one Motir seat at no charge.
s7.furtherSeats: Seats beyond the first are per user: each further person who uses Motir takes a seat at the Motir seat fee.
s7.noAiPlanSeats: An organization with no AI plan pays per user, for every seat.

s8.title: Changing plan mid-period
s8.upBody: You pay the price difference for the days left in the period, not a full new price, and receive the matching extra credits and code-graph index allowance for those days.
s8.upRenewal: Every renewal after that grants the new plan's full pool. An upgrade also clears a downgrade you scheduled earlier.
s8.downBody: Takes effect at the end of the current period, with no refund and no change to the credits or allowance you already hold. You keep your current plan until then.
s8.downClear: Upgrading again before then clears the scheduled downgrade.
s8.billingNote: The exact amount of an upgrade is shown to the owner on the billing page before they confirm.

s9.title: What changes the answer
s9.body: A gateway price change or a retired model changes the estimate, with no release of Motir.

s10.title: Invoices, security and SSO
s10.body: Standard Stripe invoicing. For security or SSO questions, <link>contact us</link>.
